1.e4 e6 2.d4 a6 3.Nf3 b5 4.Bd3.strategy: Puts the bishop on its best diagonal, where it guards e4 in advance against the bishop that Black is about to bring to b7, and eyes the b5 pawn. It does the job a knight on c3 cannot, since that would be driven off by ...b4. White keeps a compact set-up and castling in hand.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 a6 3.Nf3 b5 4.Bd3 c5.strategy: Black challenges the centre instead of waiting behind it: the d4 pawn is now attacked by the c-pawn and held only by the knight, because the bishop on d3 shuts in the queen. White has to decide how to meet the tension, and Black gets active play before castling.
